Thank you all for these thorough and critical findings. Let me synthesize what we have and propose a path forward before Monday.

First, on Daniel's title chain defect — this is the most fundamental issue. If Northlake doesn't fully own the continuation application, we can't take a meaningful exclusive license to it. I agree we should make the missing assignment a signing condition, with Daniel driving the effort with Northlake's tech transfer office immediately. If we can't get it resolved by Monday, we should consider either carving that application out of the licensed portfolio or making it a condition subsequent with a very short cure period. Daniel, please circulate your title memorandum today so we all have the details.

Second, on Sofia's royalty benchmark — a 3% rate that's 75 basis points above our validated market ceiling is significant. I recommend we go back to Northlake and renegotiate to 2.25% or below. If the business team insists on urgency and wants to keep 3%, we'll need a documented justification in the approval package, but I'd strongly prefer to push back on the rate before signing.

Third, on Martin's prior grant to the University Research Consortium — we absolutely need a carveout in the draft acknowledging their existing academic research and teaching rights. Martin, please draft that language today so we can incorporate it before Monday.

Fourth, on Nora's export-controls issue — ECCN 3A001 classification means we need provisions prohibiting transfers to military end users and requiring annual end-use screening certifications. Nora, please work with me to get those clauses drafted into the agreement this week.

All four issues need to be resolved before we sign. I'll update the approval package and the transaction checklist to reflect each of these items. Let's plan to reconvene mid-week to check progress. Does anyone disagree with this approach?

We should resolve the title issue first, or at least understand Northlake's responsiveness on the assignment, before we open the royalty renegotiation. That way we're negotiating the rate on the complete portfolio in one conversation rather than twice.

Second, Nora's point about export-controls coverage at signing is critical given the business team's desire for immediate technology access. The ECCN 3A001 provisions — military end-user prohibitions and annual end-use screening certifications — must be in the agreement at execution, not after. And Nora is right that we need drafting language that covers any future portfolio amendment so there's no compliance gap if the continuation application is added back later.

Third, Martin's carveout for the University Research Consortium needs to be precisely scoped and coordinated with Nora's export-controls provisions to avoid any ambiguity about which users and uses are covered. I appreciate Martin flagging that interaction.

Here's what I'd like each of you to bring to our mid-week check-in: Daniel, your title memorandum and an update on Northlake's responsiveness on the missing assignment. Sofia, your benchmark analysis ready to support the royalty renegotiation, with the portfolio-scope implications documented. Martin, your draft carveout language precisely scoped to the consortium's existing academic research and teaching rights. Nora, your export-controls provisions with coverage for both the current portfolio and any future amendment.

I'll escalate to the business team today to set expectations that all four issues must be resolved before Monday — and that the immediate technology access they want depends on having the export-controls provisions in place at signing. If anyone encounters resistance from Northlake or the business team on any of these items, flag it immediately so we can adjust our strategy. Any final thoughts before we adjourn?
